title: Invocation Slicer UX explorations and annotated wires
body:
Summary:

Short running notes from a set of lightweight design experiments for a token-level "Invocation Slicer" view — an exploration aimed at surfacing per-invocation token slices, their per-token cost and latency contribution, and quick remediation actions for product engineers. This doc bundles: sketches, interaction variants, prioritized backlog, and open questions for engineering tradeoffs.

Objectives:
- Let engineers answer: which token spans (prefixes/middle/suffix) drive cost or latency regressions for a route/model?
- Make hot-paths visible at a glance (heat + time) with ability to inspect raw tokens/embeddings/kv-cache hints.
- Provide low-effort remediation: toggle shorter context, switch quantized variant, or pin a faster model.
- Keep UI fast: no heavy CPU work on client, progressive hydration.

Personas / scenarios:
- SRE/on-call: triage a spike in p50/p95 latency for Chat API; needs to isolate suspect prompts that correlate with latency increase.
- ML engineer: compare two model variants on same route to understand token-level cost delta.
- Product/PM: validate whether a new system prompt causes cost increase.

Wireframe notes (low-fi):
1) Overview row (compact)
   - Route dropdown | timeframe selector | baseline model comparator toggle
   - Summary chips: avg tokens / avg cost per invocation / p95 latency / cache hit rate
2) Invocation list (left column) – lazy-loaded by score
   - Each row: short prompt preview (first 120 chars), tokens count badge, delta-cost icon, latency sparkline small, expand chevron
   - Sort modes: cost-contribution | latency | recency | severity
3) Slicer canvas (right pane)
   - Stacked microbars representing token positions; bar height encodes per-token compute cost estimate, color = latency contribution (cool->hot).
   - Hover token: tooltip shows raw token text (escaped), approx token bytes, model ops estimate, KV cache status (hit/miss), embedding size if used.
   - Click token: open side inspector with full invocation context and actions.
4) Side inspector actions
   - Quick actions: try short-context (75% truncate), toggle quantized variant, rerun sample request (sandbox), create rollback snapshot
   - Notes field: pin an observation to the route timeline (for postmortems)

Interaction alternatives considered:
- Inline token tooltips vs. dedicated inspector: tradeoff between visual density and discoverability. Chosen: concise tooltips + persistent inspector for deep ops.
- Heatmap vs stacked bars: heatmap is compact but obscures sequence. Stacked bars used to preserve token order.
- Client-side tokenization: requires shipping tokenizer libs; instead we compute tokenization server-side and stream token-aligned metadata to the client (lighter client).

Performance constraints / engineering notes:
- Token-level metadata already expensive; store precomputed per-invocation token metrics for sampled invocations only (configurable sample rate).
- For route-level rollups compute aggregated position percentiles (e.g., median cost at token index).
- Use incremental rendering: show overview + list immediately, hydrate slicer canvas when row expanded.

Backlog (prioritized):
1. MVP: invocation list + slicer canvas + hover tooltips + 3 quick actions (truncation, quantized toggle, sandbox rerun) (Q1)
2. Sampling control in Console: set sample rate per route + retention days (Q1)
3. Route-level aggregated views (percentile bands across invocations) (Q2)
4. Integration: link to Dedicated fallback policies and auto-rollout suggestions (Q2)
5. Perf: server-side precomputation job and compact delta encoding for token-level metrics (Q2)
6. UX: inline diff mode for comparing two model variants token-by-token (research spike)

Open questions / decisions needed:
- How live should this view be for high-volume routes? (prob. sampled by default; need SRE input)
- Tokenizer differences between models: canonicalization strategy? (store canonical token id plus model-specific mapping)
- Security: redaction of PII in token tooltips if invocation belongs to regulated customer. Need compliance signoff.

Notes to self (informal):
- Try a baseline microcopy: "Token heat = latency share; taller bar = higher compute cost". Test with user research.
- Prototype using 50 sampled invocations for a route and measure client render time on medium-latency network.
- Ask infra for a compact protobuf schema for token-level metrics (avoid JSON bloat).

User research script (5–10 min):
- Show problem scenario: "A spike in p95 for route /chat. Identify one invocation likely causing spike and describe remediation you'd try."
- Tasks: find a high-cost token span, take a remediation action, create a short note for the postmortem.

Appendix: sketch keys (for dev handoff)
- tokenBar.height = compute_score_normalized * 60px max; tokenBar.color = latency_percentile_to_color(token_latency_pct)
- aggregatedBand: median +/- 90th percentile ribbon
- changeAction telemetry: tag each quick action with route and sampledInvocationId for audit trail

Next steps:
- Build clickable Figma wires (Marcus) and test with 4 engineers (Luca + 3) end of next sprint.
- Create CON-2143 to track infra cost for sampling storage.
- Schedule sync with Compliance about PII redaction patterns.

---
Revision log: 2024-09-12 initial draft by Aisha; 2024-10-03 added quick-actions list (Marcus); 2024-11-18 trimmed canvas visuals (Eve); 2025-01-20 grooming update and backlog prioritization (Sofia).
